## 24 states and Washington, DC, have legalized recreational marijuana use.
### Recreational
As of April 2026, 24 states and Washington, DC, have legalized recreational marijuana.
Ohio was the latest state to legalize recreational marijuana, when voters [approved](https://com.ohio.gov/divisions-and-programs/liquor-control/renewal-existing-permit-info/guides-and-resources/adult-use-of-marijuana-in-liquor-permit-premises) Issue 2 in the November 2023 election.

These states have raised legislative measures in recent years to either begin medical or recreational legalization: [House Joint Resolution 4](https://legislature.idaho.gov/sessioninfo/2025/legislation/hjr004/) in Idaho and [Senate Bill 294](https://www.kslegislature.gov/bills/sb294/) in Kansas.

results.title: Cannabis Overview - National Conference of State Legislatures
excerpts:
# Report Cannabis Overview
## Legalization
24 states, two territories and the District of Columbia have legalized small amounts of cannabis (marijuana) for adult recreational use. Most recently, Delaware, Maryland, Minnesota, Missouri, Ohio and Rhode Island passed legislation allowing individuals 21 or older to possess certain amounts of cannabis.
With the exception of Delaware, these new laws permit individuals to home-grow marijuana—however, the number of plants one can legally cultivate varies by state. In all six of these jurisdictions, medical use cannabis was legalized prior to adult recreational use.

...

### Study Efforts
In 2020, Virginia adopted SJR 67 - having Virginia begin it's journey to join the other states in legalizing cannabis for recreational use. The resolution begins a study requiring recommendations for implementing legalization by July 1, 2022.
In 2018, study bills were filed in Hawaii, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota and Rhode Island. The measures in New Hampshire and Rhode Island were enacted and established commissions to study the legalization, regulation and taxation of marijuana.

...

## Record Clearing
As of 2023, 45 states, two territories and Washington, D.C., have record clearing laws which may apply to cannabis. Of these jurisdictions, 28 have legislation that applies specifically to record clearance of certain cannabis-related offenses.
